h1: Business systems consulting so the business doesn't run through you
intro: Every question still ends up on your phone. Jobs stall when you're on a roof or on vacation, and the way things get done depends on who is working that day. You built the business, and now you're the bottleneck in it.
definition: Business systems consulting is outside help to document how your company actually works, assign a clear owner to each part of it, and connect the tools you use, so the work gets done the same way every time without the owner stepping in.

sections.h2: What a business system really is
paras: A system is not a binder on a shelf. It's three things working together: a written process, a person who owns it, and a tool that supports it. Miss any one and the work falls back on you.

Most owner-led businesses have pieces of all three. The steps live in someone's head, ownership is assumed, and the software doesn't share information. Business systems consulting pulls those pieces together.

bullets: Documented processes for the work that repeats: answering leads, quoting, scheduling, job handoff, invoicing, collections
A clear owner for each process, written down, so nobody has to guess who handles it
Simple checklists your team will actually use, not long manuals
Connected tools: your CRM, scheduling, estimating, phones, forms and accounting sharing data so nobody retypes it
A short list of numbers that tell you whether the system is working

sections.h2: How business systems consulting works with me
paras: We start with the bottleneck that costs you the most time or money. I sit with you and your team, watch how the work moves, and write down what really happens, not what should happen. Then we fix that one process: tighten the steps, name the owner, and set up the tools to support it.

Once it holds, we move to the next one. One focused fix at a time beats a twenty-point plan nobody finishes. I work with the software you already use and don't sell any. Where practical AI or automation saves real hours, I add it.
Over the first 90 days, the goal is simple: fewer questions landing on you, and work that gets done right when you're not in the room.

sections.h2: Why the owner stops being the bottleneck
paras: Growth on top of a messy system just brings more stress. More leads mean more dropped balls and more late nights. That's why I fix the bottleneck first, then turn up the volume.

For over a decade in banking and finance, I worked with business owners through cash crunches and growing pains. Then I co-founded a company and lived it myself. I'm based in Charlotte, NC and work with owner-led businesses across the US.

faq.q: What does a business systems consultant do?
faq.a: A business systems consultant documents how your company works, assigns owners to each process, and connects the tools that support them. The aim is consistent work that doesn't depend on the owner. I start with the process causing the most pain, fix it with your team, then move to the next.

faq.q: How do I make my business run without me?
faq.a: Write down the work that repeats, give each piece a clear owner, and support it with tools that share information. Then step back and let your team run it, fixing gaps as they show up. It happens one process at a time, not all at once.

faq.q: What systems does a small business need first?
faq.a: Start with the systems closest to cash: lead handling, quoting, scheduling and invoicing. Those touch every job and every dollar. Hiring, onboarding and job handoff usually come next. Pick the one causing the most dropped balls today and fix that first.

faq.q: What is an SOP and do I need them?
faq.a: An SOP, or standard operating procedure, is a written set of steps for a task that repeats. Most small businesses need a handful, not hundreds. Short checklists for quoting, job handoff and invoicing usually do more good than a long manual nobody reads.

faq.q: Do I need new software to systemize my business?
faq.a: Usually not. Most businesses already have the tools they need, they just aren't connected or used consistently. I work with your existing CRM, scheduling, estimating and accounting tools, and only suggest something new when there is a real gap. I don't sell software, so there's no reason to push you toward any product.

faq.q: How much does business systems consulting cost?
faq.a: With Vestis Solutions, partnerships start at $3,000 a month. That includes systems work, SEO and AEO, a sales process review and four owner sessions a month. The first 90 days set the foundation, then it continues month to month. Scope is agreed on a free fit call.
